cases.meaning: Wants a better lamb pairing than a specific Malbec the table disliked.
cases.knownWrong: assistant-lexicon.ts's isNegated() only looks BACKWARD from a facet for a preceding negation word ("not X", "anything but X"). Here the negation is POSTPOSED and refers back across a relative clause ("...that Malbec they didn't love") -- "didn't" sits several content words after "Malbec", outside any backward lookback window, so grape:"Malbec" is asserted despite being the wine the guest just rejected. This is a different, harder negation shape (comparative sentiment about a previously-named wine, not a preceding refusal) and the case is annotated unanswerable:comparative for the same reason -- fixing it needs real clause-level parsing, not a lexicon addition. Deferred rather than patched around.

cases.knownWrong: assistant-query.ts's parsePrice() upper/lower detection (/\b(over|above|...)\b/) tests the regex against the WHOLE normalized query, not a window around the price figure. "friends OVER for pasta night...around $35" contains the literal word "over" as an ordinary preposition, unrelated to the price -- so the lone-figure case reads priceMin:35 (a floor) instead of banding 35 +/-20% into priceMin:28 / priceMax:42. A real, evidence-backed precision bug, but the fix (scoping the comparator check to the words near the matched amount, not the full string) touches every price pattern parsePrice handles and needs its own dedicated test pass -- not a minimal, contained change safe for this slice.
